metadata.research_goal: Research and synthesize level-based teaching, assessment, promotion, hold, and regression rules for swimming across water confidence, freestyle, other strokes, starts and turns, pacing, event readiness, open-water and triathlon needs, dryland support, and safety.

key_concepts.concept: A swim plan must gate conditioning behind water competency.
key_concepts.synthesis: Before volume, intervals, or race work, the swimmer must demonstrate safe entry and exit, face immersion, exhalation, floating, recovery to standing or stable position, and the ability to stop without panic.

key_concepts.concept: Beginner, intermediate, and advanced labels should be assigned by observed skill, not age or self-description alone.
key_concepts.synthesis: Federation learn-to-swim pathways and athlete-development models use targets, repeatability, and progressive competence. The backend should treat a user as beginner when any safety-critical gate is missing even if they are fit on land.

key_concepts.concept: Swimming skill progression depends on propulsion, drag control, and breathing timing working together.
key_concepts.synthesis: A stronger pull does not compensate for a lifted head, unstable body line, poor exhalation, or crossing the midline. Each level assessment should observe speed only after body alignment and breathing are stable.

key_concepts.concept: Promotion requires repeatable technique, not one successful length.
key_concepts.synthesis: A swimmer can move up only when the required skill survives multiple repetitions, mild fatigue, and ordinary pool distractions without safety breakdown, breath panic, or major stroke collapse.

key_concepts.concept: Freestyle is the default engine for fitness, open-water, and triathlon plans, but it must be taught as balance plus rhythm, not just arm turnover.
key_concepts.synthesis: Beginner freestyle can be short fragments; intermediate freestyle should be efficient enough for continuous aerobic work; advanced freestyle should manipulate stroke rate, distance per stroke, and event pace.

key_concepts.concept: Individual medley and advanced stroke specialization require legal, safe, and repeatable exposure to all four strokes.
key_concepts.synthesis: A swimmer should not receive IM or butterfly-heavy work until freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly basics can be performed with legal turns or appropriate developmental substitutes.

key_concepts.concept: Starts, turns, streamlines, breakouts, and underwaters are performance skills with safety gates.
key_concepts.synthesis: Pool racing readiness is incomplete without wall skills, but diving and underwater work require legal pool depth, supervision, demonstrated control, and avoidance of unsafe breath-holding practices.

key_concepts.concept: Pacing should be taught through pace-clock use, repeat consistency, stroke count, and perceived effort before hard race sets.
key_concepts.synthesis: Beginner swimmers learn easy versus hard and rest discipline. Intermediate swimmers learn repeatable 25 m to 100 m repeats. Advanced swimmers connect splits, stroke rate, stroke length, and energy-system intent.

key_concepts.concept: Open-water and triathlon readiness require environmental competence beyond pool fitness.
key_concepts.synthesis: A swimmer who can cover the race distance in a pool may still be unready for current, chop, cold, low visibility, crowd contact, navigation, wetsuit restriction, or anxiety. The backend should require open-water-specific gates.

key_concepts.concept: Dryland training supports posture, shoulder capacity, trunk control, mobility, and starts or turns; it does not replace water skill.
key_concepts.synthesis: Dryland should be scaled to the swimmer's water load and technical goals. Heavy upper-body fatigue should not precede key swim technique sessions when stroke quality is the priority.

key_concepts.concept: Shoulder, back, knee, panic, or breath-control warning signs override planned progression.
key_concepts.synthesis: Swimming is low impact but high repetition. Rapid yardage jumps, paddles, butterfly, breaststroke kick, and fatigued technique can turn manageable loads into overuse problems.

key_concepts.concept: Safety is not a beginner-only topic.
key_concepts.synthesis: Advanced swimmers still need open-water hazard checks, supervised breath-control limits, symptom reporting, lane etiquette, and event-specific rules. Confidence without safety awareness is not readiness.

technical_models.model: Three-level swimming taxonomy for app planning.

beginner.definition: Needs water confidence, basic safety, breathing, floating, gliding, and short supported or unsupported swim fragments before fitness loading.
typical_ready_tasks: front and back float with recovery
swim short front and back fragments with rest

intermediate.definition: Can swim continuous lengths safely, is learning efficient freestyle and basic stroke variety, and can handle structured aerobic practice with technique controls.
typical_ready_tasks: swim at least 25 m continuously without panic
show recognizable front crawl and backstroke
start learning pace clock and turns

advanced.definition: Can train and race with event-specific pace, legal strokes and turns, reliable starts or push-offs, load monitoring, and dryland support.
typical_ready_tasks: swim 200 m or more continuously with stable technique

technical_models.model: Water confidence progresses from comfort to survival control to automatic aquatic composure.

criteria: safe entry and exit are understood
face immersion and water on head are tolerated
bubbles or slow exhalation can be repeated
front and back floats can be entered and exited with help if needed
learner can stop, stand, hold wall, or roll to back without panic
beginner.assessment: Observe 3 to 5 short attempts, not one isolated success.

criteria: can float, tread, or scull briefly in water too deep to stand
can recover from front to back and back to front
can swim to wall or safe support after a mistake
knows basic pool rules and lane etiquette
intermediate.assessment: Include a controlled interruption such as stopping mid-length and recovering calmly.

criteria: remains calm in race warm-up, crowded lane, or open-water simulation
can adjust breathing rhythm without panic
can manage goggles leaking, missed breath, or contact without unsafe response
knows event-specific safety and stop signals
advanced.assessment: Use controlled race-context or open-water-context rehearsals with safety supervision.

technical_models.model: Freestyle develops from breathing-safe fragments to efficient aerobic stroke to event-specific speed control.

criteria: horizontal push and glide on front
arms can recover without crossing midline severely
exhalation happens underwater before turning or lifting to breathe
can swim 5 to 10 m fragments without panic
beginner.assessment: Prioritize body line, relaxed exhale, and safe stopping over distance.

criteria: can swim 25 to 100 m repeats with a mostly stable body line
breath timing causes minimal head lift
rotation comes from trunk and hips rather than rolling only the head
kick supports rhythm without exhausting the swimmer
intermediate.assessment: Use 4 x 25 m or 4 x 50 m with rest and compare stroke count, breath control, and technique decay.

criteria: can manipulate stroke rate and distance per stroke for sprint, middle-distance, distance, or open-water context
catch mechanics stay stable at race pace
fatigue does not create repeated cross-over, dropped elbow, or head-lift errors
advanced.assessment: Use race-pace repeats with split, stroke count, perceived exertion, and video cue checks.

technical_models.model: Backstroke progresses from safe supine balance to legal alternating stroke to race-ready rotation, wall awareness, and turns.

criteria: ears in water with neutral head
flutter kick can move swimmer without sitting posture
can recover to standing or wall
can travel short distance on back
beginner.assessment: Check calm breathing and body line before prescribing backstroke lengths.

criteria: body rolls without throwing head side to side
intermediate.assessment: Assess 25 m backstroke with lane-safety awareness and no collision risk.

criteria: race-legal start or in-water alternative is appropriate to context
stroke rate and rotation are coordinated
turn count and flags are used consistently
shoulder symptoms do not worsen with overhead volume
advanced.assessment: Use start or push, flags, turn, breakout, and repeat split consistency.

technical_models.model: Breaststroke requires timing and knee-safe kick mechanics before volume.

criteria: understands pull-breathe-kick-glide sequence in simple form
kick is introduced gently without forcing turnout
head and hips are coordinated enough to avoid vertical bobbing
no knee or groin pain during or after practice
beginner.assessment: Use short drill fragments and stop if knee, groin, or back discomfort appears.

criteria: can swim 10 to 25 m breaststroke with recognizable timing
kick is narrow and symmetrical enough for training
breathing does not create excessive lumbar extension
intermediate.assessment: Assess timing, knee comfort, glide, and legal turn basics before adding repeats.

criteria: stroke is legal under competition rules
pullout, breakout, and turns are coordinated
race tempo can increase without losing glide discipline
knee and groin load is tracked separately from total swim volume
event pace is practiced with symptom-free response
advanced.assessment: Use event-specific repeats with separate knee/groin response check later that day and next day.

technical_models.model: Butterfly is gated by rhythm, trunk control, shoulder capacity, and fatigue tolerance.

criteria: dolphin kick can be explored in short, low-fatigue drills
body wave is playful and non-forced
breathing does not cause panic or spinal strain
shoulder and back symptoms are absent
beginner.assessment: Use kick, body dolphin, and one-arm or drill progressions rather than full lengths.

criteria: can complete 5 to 10 m whole-stroke segments with timing intact
recovery is relaxed enough to avoid shoulder strain
breath timing does not stop forward momentum
intermediate.assessment: Prescribe short quality repetitions only while technique remains smooth.

criteria: can swim legal race-distance segments with stable rhythm
underwaters, breakout, and stroke tempo match event plan
shoulder and low-back symptoms are monitored
butterfly volume is balanced with recovery and other strokes
IM butterfly does not compromise later strokes
advanced.assessment: Use race-pace 12.5 m to 50 m segments with strict technique and symptom gates.

technical_models.model: IM readiness requires all-stroke competence plus transitions, not just willingness to attempt every stroke.

criteria: learns front crawl and backstroke first for safety and orientation
samples breaststroke kick and dolphin kick in small doses
uses stroke variety as coordination play
beginner.assessment: Confirm water confidence and basic front/back travel before adding complex stroke demands.

criteria: can perform short legal or near-legal segments of all four strokes
can complete open turns for breaststroke and butterfly
can change strokes without losing safety
understands which strokes are currently limited by pain or technique
intermediate.assessment: Use 4 x 25 m as drill or stroke segments with generous rest.

criteria: can complete 100 m IM or 200 m IM progressions with legal stroke order and turns
paces each stroke to protect the whole race
advanced.assessment: Use broken IM repeats and transition checks before continuous IM race sets.

technical_models.model: Wall skills move from safe push-offs to efficient turns to start and underwater specialization.

criteria: push and glide from wall on front and back
simple streamline position can be attempted
no diving or block starts unless directly supervised in suitable depth
beginner.assessment: Check push-off direction and ability to surface calmly.

criteria: streamline off wall for at least one body length
freestyle flip turn can be introduced if safe
underwater distance is short and supervised
intermediate.assessment: Use push-off, streamline, one or two kicks, breakout, and first stroke quality.

criteria: start, entry, streamline, underwater kicks, breakout, and first strokes are linked
turn approach and push-off are event specific
15 m underwater limit and event rules are understood
relay exchanges and backstroke starts are practiced only with appropriate supervision
breath-control work is never framed as maximum breath holding
advanced.assessment: Track time to 15 m or breakout, turn speed, distance off wall, and legal execution.

technical_models.model: Pacing progresses from perceived effort to repeat control to event-specific split planning.

criteria: can distinguish easy practice from hard effort
rests enough for breathing to settle
can stop before panic or technique collapse
beginner.assessment: Use short repeats with talk-test style breathing recovery and skill quality.

criteria: can read a pace clock or timer
can repeat 25 m or 50 m efforts within a small time range
can hold easy aerobic pace without sprint-starting each repeat
intermediate.assessment: Use 6 x 50 m or similar with target rest and compare time, stroke count, and effort.

criteria: knows goal splits for target event
can use race-pace, threshold, sprint, and recovery intensities appropriately
can alter stroke rate and distance per stroke intentionally
can execute negative, even, or controlled positive pacing depending on event
advanced.assessment: Use broken race sets, critical-speed style tests when appropriate, and stroke metric review.

technical_models.model: Event readiness combines skill legality, pace, turns, safety, and recovery capacity.

criteria: not assigned formal race events unless the event is instructional or supported
may complete short skill challenges such as 10 m, 25 m, or survival float tasks
goal is confidence and safe completion, not time
beginner.assessment: Use skill awards or simple distance milestones only after safety gates.

criteria: can complete 50 m to 200 m pool time trials only when breathing and stopping are safe
uses push starts rather than dives unless dive-ready
knows basic event rules for chosen stroke
can warm up and cool down
intermediate.assessment: Use low-pressure benchmark swims and compare technique, not only time.

criteria: event plan includes target splits, start, turns, underwaters, finish, and recovery
stroke is legal for the chosen event
training includes race-pace specificity and taper logic
meets and relays include rules awareness
advanced.assessment: Use race rehearsal sets and post-race review of split, stroke count, turn execution, and symptoms.

technical_models.model: Open-water and triathlon swimming progress from pool base to supervised exposure to race execution.

criteria: does not train alone in open water
learns floating, calm breathing, and buddy principles
uses properly fitted flotation or life jacket when appropriate for weak swimmers around natural water
does not treat race distance as the first readiness target
beginner.assessment: Confirm pool safety competence before any open-water assignment.

criteria: can swim beyond expected race distance in a pool at easy effort
practices sighting, bilateral or adaptable breathing, turns around buoys, and swimming near others in controlled settings
checks water temperature, weather, visibility, current, and access points
uses bright cap and supervised group or safety support
intermediate.assessment: Use short supervised open-water exposures before continuous race-distance rehearsal.

criteria: can execute race-specific start style, sighting rhythm, drafting, surge response, and exit transition
has practiced in similar water conditions
knows wetsuit and event equipment rules
has panic, cramp, contact, and stop-response plan
does not ignore medical or cold-water warning signs
advanced.assessment: Use race simulation with safety cover, route plan, and post-session thermal and anxiety review.

technical_models.model: Dryland scales from movement literacy to durability to event-specific power and load support.

criteria: shoulder range of motion without pain
no fatiguing upper-body circuits before swim skill sessions
beginner.assessment: Screen shoulder comfort, trunk control, and basic movement quality.

criteria: scapular control and rotator cuff endurance
basic hip hinge, squat, lunge, and landing mechanics
dryland volume does not degrade water technique
intermediate.assessment: Track soreness and shoulder response next swim session.

criteria: strength and power support starts and turns
program is synchronized with pool intensity
pull strength is balanced with shoulder health work
dryland load is reduced during taper or shoulder flare
advanced.assessment: Monitor vertical or horizontal jump, medicine-ball or pull metrics if used, and effect on pool quality.

technical_models.model: Safety criteria expand from basic water rules to event and environment management.

criteria: asks permission and uses safe entry
can float or call for help
avoids breath-hold games and deep-water tasks without readiness
beginner.assessment: Ask the swimmer to explain what they do if tired, scared, or unable to stand.

criteria: knows how to stop a set for pain or breathing distress
uses buddy system in natural water
intermediate.assessment: Check behavior during shared-lane practice and fatigue.

criteria: checks rules, environment, equipment, and emergency plan before events
does not prescribe or perform maximum underwater breath-holding
knows when to withdraw from an event
advanced.assessment: Require race-day and open-water safety checklist before event-specific plans.

technical_models.model: Beginner assessment battery for app onboarding and first four weeks.
criteria: push and glide front and back
5 to 10 m assisted or independent travel
panic or fear rating after each task
technical_models.promotion_score: Promote to intermediate only when all safety-critical tasks are independent or appropriately adapted and short travel can be repeated without panic.
technical_models.hold_score: Hold beginner if breathing, floating, or recovery skills are inconsistent.
technical_models.regression_score: Regress to water-confidence work after panic, inability to recover, or unsafe breath holding.

technical_models.model: Intermediate assessment battery for fitness, stroke development, and first event goals.
criteria: 25 m backstroke or safe back travel
4 x 25 m freestyle with repeatable rest
basic rhythmic exhale and inhale timing
front crawl stroke count can be counted
tread or float for 30 seconds if pool depth requires
open turn or safe wall turn
can follow lane direction and pass etiquette
no shoulder, back, knee, or groin symptom increase after session
technical_models.promotion_score: Promote to advanced only when the swimmer can complete structured sets and event-relevant skills with stable mechanics.
technical_models.hold_score: Hold intermediate when continuous distance is present but technique breaks down under moderate repeats.
technical_models.regression_score: Regress to beginner safety blocks if panic, floating failure, or unsafe stopping returns.

technical_models.model: Advanced assessment battery for event-specific swimming.
criteria: 200 m continuous swim or event-appropriate aerobic baseline
race-pace set for target event with split control
legal stroke and turn execution for target event
shoulder, knee, back, and fatigue monitoring
technical_models.promotion_score: Promote within advanced roles when race-specific execution improves without symptom escalation.
technical_models.hold_score: Hold advanced event work when splits improve only by losing stroke mechanics or pain increases.
technical_models.regression_score: Regress to technique or return-to-swim block after pain, unexplained fatigue, illness, or unsafe race behavior.

technical_models.model: Lane behavior and pace-clock literacy are readiness gates for structured group-style workouts.

criteria: rests at wall without blocking others
understands circle swim or lane direction
leaves at prescribed interval with simple sendoffs
can read wall clock or wearable timer
manages sendoffs, descending sets, race-pace targets, and group spacing

tactical_rules.rule: Promote a beginner to intermediate only when water safety, breathing, floating, recovery, and short continuous swimming are repeatable.
criteria: front and back float with recovery
can stop and regain safety without panic
can swim at least 25 m continuous or complete repeated 10 to 15 m lengths with stable breathing if using a smaller pool
knows basic pool rules and supervision expectations

tactical_rules.rule: Promote intermediate swimmers to advanced event training only when structured sets, stroke mechanics, pacing, and safety behavior are stable.
criteria: can swim 200 m continuous or event-relevant equivalent without panic
can complete short interval sets with planned rest
can track stroke count or split times
has a target event or advanced performance goal
reports no unmanaged shoulder, back, knee, or groin symptoms

tactical_rules.rule: Hold the current level when breath timing, exhalation, or anxiety limits safe repetition.
hold_triggers: lifting head high enough to sink hips every breath
inability to stop and float or stand safely
tactical_rules.action: Reduce distance, increase rest, return to exhale-float-glide drills, and avoid hypoxic content.

tactical_rules.rule: Regress immediately to water-confidence and supervised safety practice after a safety-critical failure.
regression_triggers: cannot recover to wall, standing, or back float
dives where diving is not permitted or not supervised
enters open water without buddy or safety support
tactical_rules.action: Stop conditioning plan, restore safety gates, and require direct instruction or supervised environment.

tactical_rules.rule: Regress stroke volume and intensity when shoulder, back, knee, groin, neck, or unusual fatigue symptoms escalate.
regression_triggers: pain above mild level during swim
pain worsens later the same day or next day
stroke mechanics change to avoid pain
rapid volume increase coincides with symptoms
paddles or stroke-specific volume aggravate symptoms
tactical_rules.action: Remove aggravating stroke or tool, reduce volume, emphasize technique and recovery, and refer to clinician when symptoms persist or are sharp.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not prescribe high-volume freestyle until breathing and body line are stable enough that fatigue does not create repeated shoulder-hostile mechanics.
tactical_rules.assessment: Watch for head lift, cross-over entry, dropped elbow, over-kicking, late breathing, and escalating shoulder or neck tension.

tactical_rules.rule: Butterfly volume stays minimal until the swimmer can keep rhythm, relaxed recovery, and trunk control while symptom-free.
tactical_rules.assessment: If timing collapses, shoulder recovery becomes strained, or low-back discomfort appears, switch to kick or single-arm drills and stop whole-stroke volume.

tactical_rules.rule: Breaststroke kick volume is progressed only when the swimmer has pain-free, narrow, controlled kick mechanics.
tactical_rules.assessment: Monitor medial knee, groin, and hip response during the session and the next day.

tactical_rules.rule: Diving starts require pool permission, safe depth, supervision, and demonstrated sitting or kneeling progression before standing or block starts.
tactical_rules.assessment: If the app cannot confirm environment and supervision, prescribe in-water or push starts only.

tactical_rules.rule: Underwater work must never be maximum breath-holding, hyperventilation, or repeated exhaustion-based hypoxic work.
tactical_rules.assessment: Use short, technical underwaters after normal breathing with supervision and full recovery; stop for dizziness, panic, or urge-to-breathe suppression behavior.

tactical_rules.rule: Introduce high-intensity sets only after the swimmer can repeat controlled easy and moderate paces without technical collapse.
tactical_rules.assessment: Use repeat-time consistency, stroke count drift, and breathing stability before adding lactate or sprint work.

tactical_rules.rule: Open-water workouts require pool competence plus supervised environmental preparation.
criteria: can swim more than planned open-water distance in pool at easy effort
can float or recover when anxious
has buddy, group, or safety craft
wears visible cap or buoy as appropriate
checks weather, water temperature, current, visibility, entry and exit, and local rules

tactical_rules.rule: Triathlon swim readiness requires race-environment rehearsal, not only pool distance fitness.
criteria: can swim near others without panic
knows start format and exit route
has practiced in wetsuit if race may require or allow it
can transition from swim exit to upright movement without disorientation

tactical_rules.rule: Do not place heavy upper-body dryland immediately before a key technique, race-pace, or high-volume swim session.
tactical_rules.assessment: If dryland causes shoulder fatigue, reduce dryland load or separate sessions so water mechanics remain high quality.

tactical_rules.rule: Paddles, fins, snorkels, pull buoys, and resistance tools are aids, not default progression shortcuts.
tactical_rules.assessment: Avoid paddles for shoulder symptoms or poor catch mechanics; avoid fins if they mask body-line problems; use tools only with a named technical purpose.

tactical_rules.rule: A swimmer is not event-ready until they understand the legal stroke, start, turn, finish, and disqualification risks for the chosen event.
tactical_rules.assessment: Use simplified rules quizzes and observed legal execution before race-specific prescriptions.

physical_demands.demand: Swimming requires body balance in a buoyant medium before propulsion can be efficient.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Beginner assessment should prioritize floating, recovery, and streamline; advanced training still protects body line under speed and fatigue.

physical_demands.demand: Breathing is constrained by water and stroke timing, making exhalation, rhythm, and anxiety control central physical skills.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Breathing instability can make a fit athlete a beginner in water; advanced swimmers use event-specific breathing plans.

physical_demands.demand: Swimming creates high repetitive shoulder exposure through overhead arm cycles.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Intermediate and advanced plans must track volume, paddles, stroke mix, and posterior shoulder endurance.

physical_demands.demand: Freestyle and backstroke need trunk rotation while butterfly, breaststroke, starts, and turns require trunk stiffness and timing.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Dryland should build anti-extension and rotation control so speed does not come from excessive lumbar motion.

physical_demands.demand: Effective kicking requires ankle mobility, plantar-flexion capacity, and rhythm without excessive energy cost.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Beginners use kick for body position; intermediate swimmers avoid over-kicking; advanced swimmers tune kick to sprint, distance, or open-water needs.

physical_demands.demand: Breaststroke stresses hip rotation, adductors, groin, and medial knee structures through repeated kick cycles.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Breaststroke progression should be symptom-gated and technique-gated, especially for intermediate swimmers adding distance.

physical_demands.demand: Starts and turns require lower-body power, streamline stiffness, rapid direction change, and breakout timing.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Advanced sprinters and pool racers need dryland and in-water power; beginners need only safe push-offs.

physical_demands.demand: Even sprint swimmers need enough aerobic capacity to recover between repeats and maintain technical quality through practice.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Intermediate fitness swimmers build steady volume gradually; advanced distance and triathlon swimmers need event-specific endurance.

physical_demands.demand: Sprint and middle-distance events require high power and tolerance of fatigue that can degrade mechanics.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Advanced swimmers use race-pace and lactate-tolerance sets only after technical and load readiness are established.

physical_demands.demand: Open water adds cold, heat, sun, chop, current, visibility, and unfamiliar exits.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Open-water progression must include environmental exposure and safety planning, not only pool distance.

physical_demands.demand: Swimmers must orient to wall, flags, lane traffic, buoys, competitors, clock, and race plan while breathing intermittently.
physical_demands.level_relevance: Pace-clock use and sighting are intermediate-to-advanced cognitive skills that strongly affect safety and performance.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Shoulder pain can emerge from high repetition, poor mechanics, load spikes, insufficient posterior shoulder endurance, or excessive paddle use.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Monitor weekly volume, intensity, paddles, and stroke mix; emphasize technique, scapular control, posterior shoulder endurance, and early symptom reporting.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Any shoulder pain that worsens during the session or remains worse next day.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Breaststroke kick can irritate medial knee, groin, or hip structures when volume or kick width exceeds tolerance.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Limit breaststroke volume, teach narrow controlled kick, avoid forcing turnout, and substitute drills or other strokes when symptoms appear.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Knee or groin symptoms during breaststroke or later that day.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Butterfly, breaststroke, poor body line, and excessive lumbar extension during breathing can irritate the low back.
warning_signs: low-back ache during butterfly or breaststroke
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use trunk control, hip mobility, technique correction, reduced butterfly or breaststroke volume, and symptom-guided progression.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Back pain that changes stroke mechanics or persists beyond normal training soreness.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High head lift or one-sided breathing overload can create neck irritation and disrupt body position.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Teach exhale before breath, rotate body, keep one goggle near water when appropriate, and balance breathing exposure without forcing bilateral patterns in unsafe fatigue.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Neck pain with repeated breathing or inability to breathe without losing balance.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hyperventilation and extended underwater breath holding can cause loss of consciousness and drowning risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Prohibit maximum breath-holding, hyperventilation, and exhaustion-based underwater tasks; use normal breathing, supervision, short technical underwaters, and full recovery.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Any unsafe breath-control behavior or dizziness.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Diving or block starts without suitable depth, supervision, skill progression, or pool permission create catastrophic injury risk.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use in-water or push starts until environment and skill are confirmed; progress from seated or kneeling entries under qualified supervision.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Uncontrolled entry, fear, head-first entry in unsafe area, or lack of supervision.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Open water introduces current, cold, chop, boat traffic, low visibility, weather change, and entry or exit hazards.
warning_signs: panic in chop or crowd contact
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use buddy or group, visible cap or buoy, weather and temperature checks, known route, safety cover, conservative exposure, and stop plan.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Panic, disorientation, shivering, cramping, or inability to sight and return safely.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Abrupt increases in weekly distance, intensity, stroke-specific volume, or dryland load increase overuse and fatigue risk.
warning_signs: sudden jump in weekly meters or yards
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Progress gradually, separate hard days, monitor session RPE and symptoms, and use recovery weeks after loading blocks.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Technique degradation across consecutive sessions or new persistent pain after a load increase.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hand paddles and resistance tools can magnify shoulder load or reinforce poor catch mechanics.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use smaller paddles or no paddles, assign technical purpose, limit volume, and remove tools during symptoms.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Any pain or worse technique when using resistance tools.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Hard sets can turn technical limitations into injury and safety risk when fatigue changes breathing, alignment, or catch.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use strict cutoffs, increase rest, reduce repeat length, and stop high-intensity sets when technical markers deteriorate.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Repeated technical failure across two or more repeats despite rest.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Dryland can harm swim quality when upper-body fatigue, soreness, or plyometric load is stacked poorly with hard pool sessions.
warning_signs: poor turns after leg power session
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Place dryland to support swim goals, reduce volume before race-pace work, and keep shoulder health work submaximal when swim load is high.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Dryland fatigue causes stroke deterioration or pain in water.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Youth swimmers may need maturation-aware progression, while masters swimmers may need longer warm-ups, recovery, and medical risk awareness.
warning_signs: adult beginner overestimates pool skill because land fitness is high
youth specializing too early in one stroke
masters swimmer ignores cardiac, medication, or cold-water risks
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use criteria-based gates, adapt volume to age and recovery, promote multi-skill development, and require medical caution when risk factors exist.
injury_or_load_risks.regression_trigger: Persistent fatigue, anxiety, medical warning signs, or recurring pain.

training_implications.implication: Beginner sessions should be rest-rich, skill-first, and supervised, with short tasks for comfort, breathing, float recovery, glides, and simple travel.
training_implications.backend_use: If level is beginner or water confidence is low, retrieve safety and breathing records before any fitness records.

training_implications.implication: Do not prescribe long continuous swims to users who cannot breathe rhythmically, float, recover, and stop safely.
training_implications.backend_use: Block high-volume workouts until water competency gates pass.

training_implications.implication: Intermediate plans should blend technique, aerobic base, simple pacing, and gradual volume rather than becoming random yardage.
training_implications.backend_use: Use main sets such as short repeat freestyle, kick and drill sets, and controlled aerobic blocks with stroke count or breathing cues.

training_implications.implication: Advanced plans should be organized around event demands: sprint speed and power, middle-distance race pace and lactate tolerance, distance economy, IM transitions, or open-water rhythm.
training_implications.backend_use: Retrieve records by target event, stroke, starts and turns, pacing model, and load risk.

training_implications.implication: Total swim volume is not enough; track freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, kick, pull, paddles, fins, and underwater volumes separately when relevant.
training_implications.backend_use: Load monitor should flag stroke-specific spikes and symptom-specific risks.

training_implications.implication: Quality sets need technical cutoffs based on stroke count, breath control, alignment, turn control, and pain.
training_implications.backend_use: Each workout should include a regression instruction such as increase rest, shorten distance, or switch to drill when technique fails.

training_implications.implication: Racing swimmers should practice starts, turns, streamlines, and breakouts frequently in small high-quality doses rather than only near race day.
training_implications.backend_use: Advanced pool-race records should include wall-skill microdoses and safety checks.

training_implications.implication: Underwater prescriptions should be written as technical streamline and breakout work, never as breath-holding contests.
training_implications.backend_use: Generated workouts must avoid phrases that imply maximum underwater distance, hypoxic challenge, or hyperventilation.

training_implications.implication: Open-water progression should move from pool base to supervised short exposure, then navigation and crowd skills, then race-specific rehearsal.
training_implications.backend_use: Open-water and triathlon retrieval must include safety plan, environment, sighting, drafting, anxiety control, and equipment context.

training_implications.implication: Dryland should be scaled to the swimmer's level and water load, with shoulder health, trunk control, mobility, and start or turn power prioritized as appropriate.
training_implications.backend_use: Pair dryland records with swim focus and symptom status; avoid hard upper-body dryland before key pool sessions.

training_implications.implication: Return-to-swim plans should restart with short easy technique work, remove paddles and high-risk strokes initially, and progress by symptom response.
training_implications.backend_use: If shoulder, back, knee, groin, panic, or long break is present, retrieve return-to-swim records instead of normal progression records.

training_implications.implication: Adult beginners may have high land fitness but low aquatic competence; water safety level should dominate initial prescription.
training_implications.backend_use: Do not infer swim level from running, cycling, gym, or general endurance history.

training_implications.implication: Youth progression should support multi-skill development, confidence, fun, and long-term participation rather than early narrow event specialization.
training_implications.backend_use: Youth swimmer plans should retrieve multi-stroke, movement literacy, and safety records before high specialization.

training_implications.implication: Masters swimmers often benefit from longer warm-ups, technical resets, recovery attention, and medical-risk-aware open-water plans.
training_implications.backend_use: Masters plans should check recent training, pain history, medications or relevant medical cautions, and event environment.

training_implications.implication: Level assessments should be repeated after a block, after a long break, or after injury, not assumed permanent.
training_implications.backend_use: Store last demonstrated swim distance, safety gate status, stroke gates, and symptom status with dates.

training_implications.implication: Workout generation should retrieve only the level, stroke, event, safety, and injury records relevant to the user.
training_implications.backend_use: Filter by level, water confidence, target event, stroke focus, pool/open-water context, session duration, equipment, and symptom history.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Water Confidence Gate
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Determine whether the user can begin skill-based pool sessions or needs supervised water-confidence work.
criteria: accepts water on face and head
recovers from front or back float
can stop and hold wall or stand safely
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Advance only after all safety-critical items are repeatable without panic.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if fear, breath holding, or inability to recover appears.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress after panic, unsafe submersion, or inability to regain safe position.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Aquatic Breathing Progression
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Teach relaxed exhalation and safe submersion before freestyle distance.
criteria: blows bubbles with mouth and nose submerged
can repeat short exhale tasks calmly
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add short swim fragments when exhale and recovery stay calm.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Stay on wall-supported breathing when exhale becomes breath holding.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to standing-water breathing if dizziness or panic appears.

backend_records_to_create.title: Float and Recover Gate
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Block unsupported deep-water work until the swimmer can float and recover.
criteria: roll front to back or back to front with support as needed
tuck or stand recovery in shallow water
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Advance to glides and short travel after repeatable recovery.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Keep support or shallow water if recovery is inconsistent.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to supported flotation after panic or failed recovery.

backend_records_to_create.title: Safe Entry and Exit Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Ensure beginner sessions start and finish with safe pool access.
criteria: uses steps, ladder, side, or teacher-approved entry
does not jump into unknown depth
exits without panic or assistance beyond planned support
knows at least two pool rules
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add jumping only after safe depth and supervision are confirmed.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if the swimmer cannot exit independently or safely.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Remove jumps or deep-water tasks after unsafe entry.

backend_records_to_create.title: Push, Glide, and Kick Introduction
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Build balance and movement before full-stroke swimming.
criteria: short flutter kick with face-in or back position
can surface or stop safely after glide
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add short freestyle fragments when glide is flat and breathing is calm.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Keep glides short if hips sink, panic appears, or swimmer cannot stop.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to wall-supported balance if glide creates fear.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Freestyle Fragment
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Introduce front crawl without turning it into a conditioning set.
criteria: uses simple side breath or roll-to-breathe strategy
stops safely at wall or standing depth
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Build to repeated 10 to 15 m fragments before 25 m continuous.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if head lift, breath panic, or frantic kick dominates.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to glide, kick, and breathing drills after repeated unsafe attempts.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Back Travel
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Use back floating and travel for safety, orientation, and confidence.
criteria: head remains still enough to keep hips near surface
can recover to standing or wall
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Progress to alternating arm backstroke when body line and recovery are safe.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if swimmer arches back, sits up, or cannot see wall safely.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to supported back float if fear or collision risk is high.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Pool Safety Rules
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Attach safety context to every beginner plan.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Safety rules remain active after promotion.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold all progression when safety behavior is unreliable.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress to supervised safety lesson after unsafe behavior.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Dryland Support
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Provide low-fatigue movement prep for new swimmers.
criteria: no hard upper-body fatigue before pool skill
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add strength only when pool skill quality is not compromised.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold dryland progression if soreness disrupts swim learning.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce to mobility and breathing if shoulder or back symptoms appear.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner to Intermediate Promotion Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Central rule for level transition in backend progression engine.
criteria: 25 m continuous swim or repeatable short-pool equivalent
no panic response to missed breath
knows lane and pool safety basics
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Promote when criteria are repeated on at least two separate sessions or clearly demonstrated in assessment.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold beginner if any safety-critical criterion is missing.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress after safety failure, panic, or long break that removes confidence.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Freestyle Efficiency
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Build sustainable front crawl for fitness, sport support, and event base.
criteria: breath timing without large head lift
kick supports rhythm rather than panic
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Advance when repeat times and stroke count are controlled with good breathing.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if speed gains come from frantic kicking or poor shoulder mechanics.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to drill and shorter repeats when stroke count spikes or breathing fails.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Breathing Control
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Assess readiness for aerobic sets and open-water progression.
criteria: can breathe both sides or adapt side as needed without panic
can recover at wall between repeats
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add longer aerobic repeats after breathing remains stable across a set.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if swimmer breath-holds, gasps, or cannot recover between repeats.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to short technique repeats after anxiety or dizziness.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Continuous Swim Base
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Determine whether the user can receive structured fitness swimming.
criteria: swims 100 to 200 m continuous at easy effort
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Use continuous distance as one input for advanced promotion, not the only input.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if continuous distance is possible only through survival stroke or panic pace.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to interval format after long break or technique collapse.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Backstroke Development
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Develop backstroke for stroke variety, recovery, and competition pathway.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add turns and pacing after body line and wall awareness are consistent.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if collision risk or low-back arching appears.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Use back kick and drill work after symptoms or orientation errors.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Breaststroke Development
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Teach timing and narrow kick with knee/groin safeguards.
criteria: 10 to 25 m breaststroke with recognizable timing
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add breaststroke repeats only after technique and symptoms are stable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if kick is wide, asymmetrical, or painful.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Remove breaststroke kick volume after knee or groin symptoms.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Butterfly Introduction
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Introduce butterfly safely without high-volume fatigue.
criteria: body wave without forced lumbar extension
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Progress by quality of short segments, not total butterfly distance.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if rhythm collapses or recovery strains shoulders.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to kick and one-arm drills after technique or symptom failure.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Turns Introduction
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Introduce wall skills without unsafe diving or breath-holding.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add speed only after turn control and breakout breathing are safe.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if disorientation or breath panic occurs.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to touch-turn-push-off drills after failed turn attempts.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Pacing Introduction
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Teach repeat consistency before race-pace intensity.
criteria: can use wall clock or timer
can repeat 25 m or 50 m efforts
can avoid sprinting the first repeat of every set
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add threshold or race-pace work when repeat control is reliable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if effort control is absent or technique collapses at moderate pace.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to rest-rich technique intervals after repeated pacing failure.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Open-Water Introduction
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Decide whether an intermediate swimmer can begin supervised open-water exposure.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add short open-water sessions only with safety support and conservative exposure.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold in pool if anxiety, poor sighting, or no safety support exists.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to pool after panic, cold distress, or disorientation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Triathlon Swim Base
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Prepare a first triathlon swimmer without skipping open-water safety.
criteria: can swim race distance plus safety margin in pool at easy effort
can sight without full stop in drills
knows race start and exit plan
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Move to race rehearsal after supervised open-water exposures are successful.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if pool distance exists but anxiety or sighting is poor.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to pool and anxiety-control drills after open-water panic.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Dryland Durability
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Support increasing swim volume with shoulder and trunk capacity.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase dryland when it supports pool quality and recovery.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if dryland soreness disrupts technique.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce dryland after shoulder, back, or knee symptom increase.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate Load Monitoring
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Prevent rapid volume and tool overload during progression.
criteria: shoulder, back, knee, groin symptom trend
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Progress volume only when symptoms and technique are stable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold progression after load spike or rising soreness.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce volume and remove aggravating tools after symptom escalation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Intermediate to Advanced Promotion Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Central rule for enabling race-pace and event-specific swimming.
criteria: 200 m continuous swim or event-equivalent base
can use pace clock or split timer
turn and wall safety are dependable
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Promote after two or more successful structured sessions or formal assessment.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if only distance is present but pacing, turns, or symptoms are not ready.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress to intermediate technique or return-to-swim after pain, long break, illness, or safety issue.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Freestyle Race-Pace Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Build race-pace sets for sprint, middle-distance, distance, or open-water freestyle.
criteria: stroke count or stroke rate tracked
turn and breakout included for pool events
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase race-pace density only when split and mechanics hold.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if speed requires stroke collapse or unsafe breath control.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to technique pace after repeated failures.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Stroke Specialization Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Support backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, and IM specialists.
criteria: symptom gates for shoulder, back, knee, or groin
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Specialize only after all-stroke foundation and target-stroke legality are adequate.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold specialization when load is tolerated only at low volume.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce target-stroke volume after symptoms or legal breakdown.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Start Specialization
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Add legal, supervised starts for racing swimmers.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Move from in-water or push start to dive progression only when environment and skill are confirmed.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold at push starts if context is unknown.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to lower start progression after uncontrolled entry.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Turns and Underwaters
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Train wall performance without unsafe breath-holding.
criteria: breakout before technique or oxygen stress
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase speed or underwater quality only when breath and breakout remain safe.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if turn speed creates disorientation.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Shorten underwater and slow turn after dizziness, panic, or poor breakout.

backend_records_to_create.title: 50 m and 100 m Sprint Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Gate sprint event training and race rehearsal.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase sprint density only when speed remains technically clean.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if sprint work turns into sloppy fatigue volume.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to short technique speed after shoulder pain or repeated form failure.

backend_records_to_create.title: 100 m and 200 m Middle-Distance Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Build race-pace and lactate-tolerance work for middle-distance swimmers.
criteria: can hold target split in broken reps
knows first and second half plan
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add lactate sets after race-pace mechanics are stable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if fatigue causes unsafe turns or major breathing disruption.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to aerobic and technique support after unresolved fatigue.

backend_records_to_create.title: 400 m to 1500 m Distance Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Build distance events around economy, pacing, and durable technique.
criteria: stroke count and breathing remain efficient
nutrition and hydration context considered for long sessions
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase distance pace work after stable repeat economy.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if volume increases degrade mechanics or shoulder symptoms.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce distance and add drill resets after technique collapse.

backend_records_to_create.title: Individual Medley Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Gate IM training behind all-stroke and transition competence.
criteria: legal or coach-approved developmental four-stroke execution
butterfly and breaststroke symptom gates passed
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Add continuous IM sets only after broken IM is technically stable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if one stroke is unsafe or illegal under fatigue.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to stroke-specific drills for the limiting stroke.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Open-Water Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Prepare open-water swimmers for race or long continuous swims.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase distance or race specificity only after successful exposure in similar conditions.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if environment differs substantially from training.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to shorter supervised exposures after panic, cold distress, or navigation failure.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Triathlon Swim Readiness
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Link swim training to triathlon race execution.
criteria: panic, cramp, and contact response plan
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Race-ready only after race-like swim rehearsal with safety support.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if the athlete can swim pool distance but not handle contact, sighting, or environment.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to pool and short open-water exposures after adverse race simulation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Dryland Power Support
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Support starts, turns, posture, and stroke durability.
criteria: lower-body power for starts and turns
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase power work only when landings and shoulder response are good.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if dryland impairs race-pace water quality.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce load during taper, pain flare, or high swim intensity weeks.

backend_records_to_create.title: Advanced Taper and Race Week Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Reduce fatigue while preserving feel, speed, and race skills.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Use sharper race rehearsal only when freshness improves technique.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold new technical changes during race week unless safety-related.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce intensity after illness, pain, or excessive fatigue.

backend_records_to_create.title: Hypoxic Blackout Guardrail
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Prevent unsafe generated breath-control workouts.
criteria: no repeated underwater work under fatigue
short technical underwaters only when appropriate and supervised
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: No promotion changes this rule; it is always active.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold any underwater progression when supervision or readiness is unclear.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress after dizziness, panic, or unsafe breath-control behavior.

backend_records_to_create.title: Dive Start Guardrail
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Prevent unsafe dive prescriptions.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Advance from push to dive progression only after context and skill are confirmed.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Use push starts when any context is unknown.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Remove dive work after fear, poor control, or unsafe environment.

backend_records_to_create.title: Open-Water Safety Checklist
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Attach mandatory safety checks to open-water and triathlon prescriptions.
criteria: buddy, group, coach, or safety craft
visible cap or buoy as appropriate
current, tides, boat traffic, and visibility checked
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Increase exposure only when checklist is satisfied and prior exposure was calm.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold open-water work if safety support or conditions are unknown.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to pool after unsafe conditions or failed safety response.

backend_records_to_create.title: Equipment Tool Progression Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Control paddles, fins, pull buoy, snorkel, and resistance use.
criteria: tool has a clear technical purpose
tool does not hide poor body line
tool does not increase unsafe breath-control behavior
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Use tools after base skill exists and symptoms are quiet.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold tool progression when technique worsens.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Remove tool after pain or unsafe compensation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return-to-Swim Regression Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Route users returning from injury, illness, or long break away from normal progression.
criteria: limited butterfly and breaststroke kick if relevant
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Resume normal level only after several symptom-stable sessions.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold return block while pain or anxiety response is variable.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce to water confidence or clinician-guided rehab after symptom escalation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimming Level Assessment Scoring
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Score level from safety, technical, endurance, pacing, event, and symptom domains.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: All safety gates plus most level-specific gates must be met; event-specific gates apply only to relevant goals.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold when safety passes but technical or load criteria are inconsistent.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress when safety gate, symptom gate, or recent ability is lost.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimming Retrieval Tags
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Select compact context for workout generation.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Retrieve advanced records only when advanced gates pass for that domain.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Retrieve hold rules when any key readiness field is missing.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Retrieve return-to-swim or beginner safety records after symptoms, long break, or confidence loss.

backend_records_to_create.title: Youth Swimming Adaptation Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Avoid adult-style volume plans for youth without development context.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Promote by demonstrated skill and confidence, not race results alone.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold specialization if broad foundation or enjoyment is missing.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Reduce load after pain, burnout signs, or repeated fear.

backend_records_to_create.title: Masters Swimming Adaptation Rule
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Adapt level rules for adult and masters swimmers.
criteria: current water skill over past experience
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Promote by current demonstration, not old race history.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold if cardiovascular, medication, pain, or confidence concerns are unresolved.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress after long break, illness, or new safety concern.

backend_records_to_create.title: Event Rule Awareness Gate
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Ensure competition workouts include legal execution context.
criteria: relay or IM order understood if relevant
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Enable race-specific prescription when rules and execution are adequate.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold race rehearsal if the athlete cannot explain or perform the legal basics.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Return to skill teaching after repeated legal errors.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimming Symptom Dashboard
backend_records_to_create.app_use: Store swimmer-specific load and symptom fields for progression decisions.
backend_records_to_create.promotion_rule: Progress only when dashboard fields are stable.
backend_records_to_create.hold_rule: Hold after meaningful load spike or symptom increase.
backend_records_to_create.regression_rule: Regress to return-to-swim after repeated symptom alerts.
